_about: Cause of each of the five worst failures in REPORT.md section 5, diagnosed by looking at the frame, the on-device OCR and the ground truth (2026-11-27). Keyed '<frame key>#<field>'.
5038830a-c28b-49ca-b218-0664267c8ed4/022: Dropped one narrow character: the suffix is ~3 px per letter at the 480x640 Mock Device Kit resolution and the 'I' in 'QILN' vanished. The phone's own OCR read 'MC2844SPB.DBKQILN' correctly on this frame, so an OCR-disagreement check would have flagged it; the model's confidence (0.90) did not.
e6c515fe-9406-4401-a2fd-ab8fef2b78be/956: Ground-truth ambiguity, not a reading error: the break is in the wall just under the ceiling slab (labelled 'wall'), and the technician said 'broken ceiling', which the app passed on as the surface. The model followed the spoken surface.
e6c515fe-9406-4401-a2fd-ab8fef2b78be/968: Two values in one box: the SERIAL NO. field has a printed 'G155' and a white sticker '091605027'. The truth takes both; the model took the sticker only. Plate mounted upside down; the model read it correctly otherwise.
e6c515fe-9406-4401-a2fd-ab8fef2b78be/f4c: Label ambiguity: the technician called it seepage (labelled water_stain), but what is visible is blue paint and plaster flaking off a damp wall, which is what the model named (peeling_bubbling_paint). Both describe this wall; the taxonomy forces one.
cef9110b-e21c-4137-a638-6d8df24ee586/f75: Different target: the truth is the broken ventilator (surface 'window', the nearest category for a wall opening); the model described the water-streaked wall below it ('wall'). The same mismatch drives its size estimate (56-80 sq ft vs a 35x35 cm opening).
